title: Big Fish in an Expanding Pond
summary: This article details the rise of Canopy Growth Corp., parent company of Tweed, to become the world's largest cannabis business. It highlights co-founder Bruce Linton's unique business approach, focusing on market share over immediate profit, meticulous standard operating procedures, and strategic partnerships for global expansion. The company's efforts to establish credibility with doctors and prioritize customer care are also discussed, alongside its preparations for Canada's recreational cannabis market.

title: Here’s Who Is Expected to Buy the Cabela’s Sporting Goods Chain
summary: A consortium comprising Bass Pro Shops, Goldman Sachs Group's private equity arm, and Capital One Financial Corp is reportedly in the lead to acquire outdoor gear retailer Cabela's. The deal is expected to unite two major hunting and fishing retailers, valuing Cabela's at well over $4 billion, and has prevailed over a rival bid from Sycamore Partners and Synchrony Financial. The acquisition follows Cabela's exploration of strategic alternatives under pressure from activist fund Elliott Management Corp.

title: Microsoft Azure goes to Paris
summary: Microsoft announced plans to open a new Azure data center farm in Paris, following Amazon Web Services' similar announcement. This expansion is part of Microsoft's global cloud capacity building, doubling its Azure capacity in Europe in the past year. The move addresses data sovereignty and compliance needs in European countries, with the new facilities expected to come online in 2017.

title: Brandon Abbey is Back - Former Escrow.com President Helping Payoneer Make Push Into Domain Space
summary: Brandon Abbey, former President of Escrow.com, has joined Payoneer as Senior Advisor to help the financial services company expand its presence in the domain escrow market. Payoneer, a global payments firm, acquired Armor Payments earlier this year and is now offering escrow services for the domain industry, aiming to become a leading provider. Abbey, leveraging his extensive experience, is focused on developing features like domain holding and credit card payments to cater to buyers, sellers, and brokers.

title: Exclusive Interview: Payoneer CEO Sees Brexit May Have Effect on Cost Structure
summary: In an exclusive interview, Payoneer CEO Scott Galit discusses the company's focus on cross-border B2B payments, its acquisition strategy including Armor Payments, and its global client base which includes companies like Google and Amazon. He highlights Payoneer's commitment to compliance and outlines future plans amidst the evolving landscape of digital payments, including the potential impact of Brexit on its cost structure. Galit emphasizes the company culture as its greatest competitive advantage in a crowded market.

title: The 9 Best ETFs for Retail Power
summary: This article identifies nine top Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) that offer exposure to the retail sector, particularly highlighted for the traditionally strong fourth quarter. It details various retail-focused ETFs, from broad market-cap weighted funds to those concentrating on online retail or specific countries, explaining their holdings, expense ratios, and investment strategies. The article provides investors with a diverse selection of ETFs for capitalizing on retail sector performance.

title: Digital Payment Firm Payoneer Raises $180M
summary: Digital payments firm Payoneer has raised $180 million, marking it as the largest investment in an Israeli FinTech company and one of the biggest financing rounds in Israel recently. This round, led by Technology Crossover Ventures (TCV), included $90 million for company expansion and $90 million from existing shareholders. The investment is seen as a potential last private funding round before an IPO for Payoneer, which currently serves 3 million businesses in 200 countries, competing with major players like PayPal.

title: Garmin co-founder is only one from KC area to make Forbes 400 mega-rich list
summary: Garmin co-founder Min Kao is the only Kansas City area resident to make the 2016 Forbes 400 list, ranking 246th with a net worth of $2.7 billion. Other notable changes in the list include Charles and David Koch falling to 7th place, Warren Buffett dropping to 3rd, and Donald Trump's net worth decreasing due to a softening real estate market. Bill Gates maintained his position as the richest American.

title: American Express Is the Latest Big Name to Upgrade Its Parental Leave Policy
summary: American Express has announced an upgraded parental leave policy offering up to 20 weeks of paid leave, joining a growing trend among large corporations. This move reflects a broader shift towards valuing work-life balance and using generous parental leave as a benefit to attract skilled workers. However, this trend is primarily seen in large companies for high-wage earners, as smaller businesses often cannot afford similar benefits.

title: E-payment firm ACI opens Limerick, Ireland data center
summary: Electronic payment and banking solutions company ACI Worldwide has opened its European data center in Limerick, Ireland, creating 50 new jobs and expanding its existing team. This fully redundant facility highlights Ireland's appeal for data center investment due to low taxes, strong privacy, and good fiber links. The move was supported by IDA Ireland and various political figures, emphasizing the long-term commitment and value of hosting data centers in the region.

title: Lear opens Innovation Center in Capitol Park downtown Detroit
summary: Lear Corp. has opened a $10 million Innovation Center in downtown Detroit's Capitol Park district, bringing highly skilled jobs and providing paid internships for university students. The center, located in a renovated 129-year-old building, will serve as a hub for future auto interior ideas and a business incubator. Lear CEO Matt Simoncini spearheaded the move to leverage downtown Detroit's universities and growing vibrancy for business opportunities.

title: Louis Vuitton’s luxury goods are not available on Amazon -- and that’s smart
summary: Louis Vuitton's parent company, LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE, has chosen not to sell its luxury goods on Amazon, a strategy experts believe is smart to protect the brand's image. Despite slow sales growth in some high-end fashion brands, the company is maintaining its stance against e-commerce giant Amazon. This decision aims to prevent brand damage that could occur from selling luxury items too soon on a mass-market platform.

title: Why Corbus Pharmaceuticals Holdings Inc Jumped Higher Today
summary: Corbus Pharmaceuticals' stock rose over 13% today in anticipation of its CEO appearing on Jim Cramer's Mad Money. The company is developing Resunab, an anti-inflammatory drug, and currently has it in three phase 2 clinical trials with results for systemic sclerosis expected by year-end. Positive outcomes could validate the drug for other conditions like cystic fibrosis and dermatomyositis, influencing its future valuation.

title: Enec Announces ‘Formal Closing’ Of $24.4Bn Financial Package For Barakah
summary: The Emirates Nuclear Energy Corporation (Enec) and Korea Electric Power Corporation (Kepco) have formally closed a $24.4 billion financing package for the Barakah nuclear station in Abu Dhabi. This financing involves direct loans and equity commitments from Enec, Kepco, and several banks, ensuring funds for the construction and commissioning of the four-unit facility. The Barakah station, scheduled for completion in 2020, is expected to supply a quarter of the UAE’s electricity needs.

title: Bartolotta cooks up kitchen for Kohl's
summary: Bartolotta Restaurant Group partnered with Kohl's Corp. to create "The Kitch," a 32,000-square-foot dining area at Kohl's corporate headquarters in Menomonee Falls. This initiative aims to attract and retain employees by offering high-quality meal services, a trend seen in tech and financial sectors. The move is a strategic diversification for Bartolotta and a significant upgrade for Kohl's in employee amenities, despite its substantial investment.

title: Hershey Trusts Microsoft Cloud To Power Digital Transformation
summary: Hershey has adopted Microsoft's Azure cloud and Office 365 for its digital transformation efforts, driven by CIO Carlos Amesquita. This move allows the global company to enhance collaboration, utilize IoT sensors for manufacturing data analysis via Cortana Intelligence Suite, and leverage Microsoft's hybrid cloud approach for strategic business decisions and improved efficiency. Microsoft's cloud success, highlighted by its recent stock performance, is attributed to its global presence, trusted brand, and flexible hybrid solutions appealing to large customers like Hershey.

title: Cyber attacks disrupt PayPal, Twitter, other sites
summary: Hackers launched a sophisticated distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack using an army of internet-connected devices, including webcams and digital recorders, to disrupt major websites like Twitter, PayPal, and Spotify. The attacks targeted Dyn, an internet infrastructure company, causing widespread outages in the US and Europe. Authorities are investigating this significant breach of internet stability, highlighting vulnerabilities in Internet of Things devices.

title: Behind the Fidelity Blue Chip Growth Fund’s Disappointing Performance in 2016
summary: The Fidelity Blue Chip Growth Fund (FBGRX) had a below-average performance in 2016, placing seventh among 12 peer funds for point-to-point returns. While tech, energy, and consumer discretionary sectors contributed positively, healthcare, industrials, and materials significantly dragged down the fund's overall performance. This prompted a call for investors to carefully review their allocations to FBGRX.

title: AT&T sets $35 rate for online TV, will test a la carte plans
summary: AT&T announced a new online-streaming TV service called DirecTV Now priced at $35 a month for over 100 channels, launching next month. The company also stated intentions to potentially experiment with a la carte programming options, aiming to compete with existing online TV providers and demonstrate consumer benefits amidst its proposed merger with Time Warner Inc. This move is a response to customer migration to lower-priced online alternatives and part of AT&T's strategy to bolster its maturing wireless business.

title: SK Telecom’s NUGU AI Service a Hit with Consumers
summary: SK Telecom's NUGU AI speaker/lamp service has seen a significant increase in sales, nearly doubling daily since mid-October. The company strategically discounted the product to build a large user base, aiming to leverage its cloud-based deep-learning technology for continuous service improvement. SKT plans future updates for NUGU, including a potential food delivery service, and established "Nuguna Corporation" to gather user feedback.

title: Groupon Buys LivingSocial as Rival Daily-Deals Providers Unite
summary: Groupon has acquired rival daily-deals site LivingSocial for an undisclosed amount, with the deal expected to close next month. Groupon CEO Rich Williams believes the acquisition will add approximately 1 million active customers to Groupon's existing 29.1 million users. LivingSocial, once valued at $1 billion, has seen its value decline significantly, leading to layoffs and Amazon ceasing its investment in the company.

title: Google parent company Alphabet’s profit surges on mobile, video ads
summary: Alphabet, Google's parent company, reported a 27 percent increase in net income to $5.06 billion, with revenue jumping 20 percent to $22.45 billion, driven by strong mobile and video advertising, particularly from YouTube. The company also announced a $7 billion stock repurchase and highlighted its advancements in mobile advertising and new product launches like Google Assistant and Google Home. Analysts noted the successful transition to mobile and the potential for new growth areas like cloud services, despite a fall in cost-per-click.
